name: App A3: AEP → MotionDoc converter for 3D (model3d, stage3d world, actors, props)
description: Extends the A2 converter so the director's 3D layers play on the engine's three layer: model3d product shots (the label can), and the cartoon world (stage3d with its actor3d and prop3d members: camera, lights, ground, backdrop, glTF actors with a clip and blocking marks, props). Toon shading, curved walls and bone attach become warnings for later work.

userStories.title: model3d → three layer (primitive can with label, glTF, view rotation, camera fit)
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want the 3D product shot to turn on the new engine so that product films keep their hero moment.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'model3d' and shared/aep/layer.ts (aepModel3D* schemas: viewport, source, textures, material, view, lighting, shadow, camera).

Create web/src/motion/aep/model3d.ts exporting convertModel3D(layer, ctx) returning a three layer: size from viewport, transparent background, base transform from A2's baseLayer, lighting preset, shadow opacity, one object: a cylinder for source.shape 'can' (radius 0.5, height proportions.height) with material.map = textures.label and color = textures.side, or a gltf object for a gltf source; view.rotation (keyframed [x,y,z] degrees) → object rotation.x/y/z tweens; camera.fov kept and camera.position.z chosen so the object height × camera.fit fills the viewport height (z = h*fit / (2*tan(fov/2))).
Wire it into convertLayers in convert.ts in place of the A2 warning.
Create web/src/motion/aep/model3d.test.ts with the stored 'hero:product3d' layer shape.
acceptanceCriteria: The stored product3d layer converts to a three layer 441x1296 with one cylinder object of height 3.075 whose material.map is the label asset
Its view.rotation keyframes [4,-18,0] -> [4,18,0] over 120 frames give a tween on object:<id> 'rotation.y' from -18 to 18 over 4 s
camera.position.z equals 3.075 * 1.5 / (2 * tan(15°)) within 1e-6 for fov 30, fit 1.5
The converted doc passes parseMotionDoc and validateTargets
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: stage3d world → three layer (camera, lights, ground, backdrop)
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want the cartoon set to appear (floor, painted backdrop, lighting) so that the characters have a world to stand in.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'stage3d' and shared/aep/layer.ts (aepStageCameraSchema, aepStageSetSchema, aepStageLightsSchema, aepStageStyleSchema).

Create web/src/motion/aep/stage3d.ts exporting convertWorld(world, members, ctx): a three layer of viewport size with camera position/target(lookAt)/fov, lighting preset (unknown → 'studio' + warning), a ground plane object (groundSize, rotation [-90,0,0], material.color = set.ground) and, when set.backdrop is set, a backdrop plane with material.map = the backdrop image at z = -wall.distance, sized wall.height tall with the image aspect; curve and style.shading 'toon' / outline add one warning each.
In convert.ts, for each stage3d layer collect the layers of the same list whose stage equals its id as members and remove them from the 2D list.
Create web/src/motion/aep/stage3d.test.ts with a world copied from a stored cartoon film.
acceptanceCriteria: The stored 'wake:world' converts to one three layer 1920x1080 with camera position [0,1.7,7.4], lookAt [0,0.9,0], fov 35 and lighting preset 'golden'
It has a ground plane of size [16,8] coloured '#dbcebb' and a backdrop plane whose material.map is the backdrop image asset
Its actor3d and prop3d members no longer appear as separate layers or warnings in the converted 2D list
Toon style adds exactly one warning naming the world id
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: actor3d members: glTF actors with a clip and blocking marks
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want the characters standing on their marks and moving between them so that the cartoon shots read.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'actor3d' and shared/aep/layer.ts (actor3d: assetId, height, marks, clips) and engine/src/schema/layer3d.ts (gltf geometry height, Animation3D).

Add convertActor(actor, ctx) to stage3d.ts: a gltf object (asset from assetId, height default 1.0), position [marks.x, 0, marks.z], rotation [0, facing, 0]; keyframed marks → object position.x / position.z / rotation.y tweens via propertyTweens; clips[0] → animation { clip: name, loop, offset: startFrame / fps }; more than one clip → warning (only the first plays).
Add tests to stage3d.test.ts using the stored 'first-sip:pip' actor and one actor with keyframed marks if a stored film has one (else a hand-made one).
acceptanceCriteria: The stored pip actor (marks [0,0,0], clips [{ name: 'Idle', startFrame: 0, loop: true }]) converts to a gltf object with animation clip 'Idle', loop true, offset 0, at position [0,0,0]
Keyframed marks [0,0,0] -> [2,1,90] over frames 0..60 give tweens on position.x 0 -> 2, position.z 0 -> 1 and rotation.y 0 -> 90 over 2 s
An actor with two clips gives one warning naming the actor and the dropped clip
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: prop3d members: glTF and primitive props, product role, attach fallback
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want the props and the product in the scene so that the set is dressed and the product is visible.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'prop3d' and shared/aep/layer.ts (prop3d: source, size, position, rotation, scale, role, attach, textures).

Add convertProp(prop, actors, ctx) to stage3d.ts: gltf source → gltf object with height = size; primitive source → the matching primitive (reuse model3d's mapping); card source → plane with textures.front as map; position/rotation/scale (keyframed → tweens); attach { actor } → position = that actor's position + [0.25, 0.9 × actor height, 0] with one warning; keep the engine's 50-object limit (drop extras with a warning).
Add tests to stage3d.test.ts with the stored 'first-sip:counter' and 'first-sip:cold-brew' props.
acceptanceCriteria: The stored counter prop converts to a gltf object with geometry height 0.6 at position [1.5,0,0]
The attached cold-brew prop is placed at pip's position + [0.25, 0.9, 0] and adds one warning naming 'first-sip:cold-brew' and the bone
A world with 60 props converts to at most 50 objects and one warning
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Golden test covers 3D films; browser check of one cartoon and one product film
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want every stored film, 3D included, to convert and the two 3D kinds to look right on the dev page.
steps: Make films.test.ts assert zero 'skipped' warnings for model3d, stage3d, actor3d and prop3d kinds across all stored films (other warnings are allowed and counted).

Open http://localhost:5173/aep-motion.html?film=<id> with headless Chromium for one film with a stage3d layer and one with a model3d layer (find them with a node script over data/films), save screenshots at 25 % and 75 % to debug/app/ and record what you saw in notes.
acceptanceCriteria: films.test.ts passes on every stored film with no 3D 'skipped' warnings
The cartoon screenshot shows the ground, the backdrop and at least one character; the product screenshot shows the can, and the 25 % and 75 % frames differ
notes names the film ids and screenshots and lists the remaining warning kinds with counts
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`

shared/aep/layer.ts (model3d, stage3d, actor3d, prop3d schemas) and shared/aep/stage3d.ts
metadata.standingRule: Engine PRD. Everything is offline and free: unit tests in vitest (jsdom project) and browser checks on the engine lab pages. The director app is not changed.
guardrails: Work offline. The only network use allowed is `npm install`. Tests never fetch; use the stored films under data/films/*/versions/*.json (read with node:fs) and assets under web/public.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md and engine/docs/README.md before writing code. The spec is the contract: if it is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in notes.
The app's composition format is AepCompositionJson from `@shared/aep` (our own copy of the schema). Never import `reacthub-pixitweenjs`, `pixi.js`, `@pixi/*` or `pixi-filters` in new code.

Use the engine through `@engine/*` (engine/src). Do not edit engine/ except the files in metadata.sharedEdits; if the engine lacks something, add a row to docs/todos/ENGINE-NEEDS.md, use a workaround and say so in notes.
Edit only the files the story names, their tests, and metadata.sharedEdits. Do not change server/ behaviour, agent prompts or stored films.
No `@ts-nocheck` and no `@ts-ignore`. `@ts-expect-error` only with a reason on the same line.
jsdom has no 2D canvas context and no WebGL: unit-test pure logic; check drawing in the browser. Never weaken a test to make it pass.

Debug output and screenshots go to debug/app/ (gitignored). For a browser check use the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (already running; do not start another); headless Chromium through @playwright/test is fine.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements or test output.

`npm test` has 11 known failures outside your files (10 in scripts/preflight/docs.test.ts, 1 in web/src/authoring-agreement.test.tsx). Do not edit those files. The `npm test` gate passes when no other test fails.
3D values are metres and degrees in both formats; convert only units the spec names. Keep every converted three layer within the engine limits (50 objects, 6 lights, 16..2048 px).

The dev server on http://localhost:5173 is owner-run and shared: never kill, restart or stop it (no kill/pkill/lsof-kill on vite or port 5173). If it is down, use headless Chromium against `npx vite --config web/vite.config.ts --port 5180 --strictPort` started and stopped by you, and only that one.
